title: Evaluator-Optimizer Loops: Why the Best Agents Grade Their Own Work
summary: One LLM call generates a candidate response; a second call — sometimes the same model with a different prompt, sometimes a separate, cheaper model — evaluates it against explicit, written-out criteria and returns structured feedback. The loop repeats until the evaluator passes it or a retry budget runs out. It works well precisely where quality is easy to critique but hard to specify as a single instruction up front: code that has to pass tests, translations that have to preserve nuance, copy that has to hit a tone. The generator gets to be loose and fast; the evaluator carries the actual bar.
key_learning: This site's own daily pipeline uses a lightweight version of this: the CI workflow (see .github/workflows/validate-content.yml) is a mechanical evaluator that checks each new daily entry against a schema before it's considered valid — a cheap, deterministic stand-in for a full LLM evaluator, useful precisely because the criteria (required fields, valid JSON, valid date) are fully specifiable.
